answer: Proof-of-personhood escrow is one concrete defense: before transacting, each agent must register a hardware-rooted identity and stake a bond. The protocol samples prior ledger history as a river of attestations, and a newcomer's first outputs must reference that kernel of verified work. Faking a thousand agents means procuring a thousand distinct roots and bonding each one, and any colluding cluster is slashed once peers detect duplicated behaviour. The attacker faces the full ocean of collateral at risk, while honest agents reclaim their stake after consistent, independent attestation.
